name: Melanoma of Soft Tissue

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Soft Tissue Melanoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant melanocytic cells in soft tissue biopsy with characteristic morphology
Positive staining for melanocytic markers such as S-100, HMB-45, and Melan-A
No evidence of primary cutaneous or mucosal melanoma after thorough clinical and imaging evaluation
Detection of mutations commonly associated with melanoma (e.g., BRAF, NRAS) supports diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant melanocytic cells in soft tissue with positive immunohistochemical markers and exclusion of primary cutaneous or mucosal melanoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pathology, dermatology, and radiology.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pigmented soft tissue mass with irregular borders
pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as a darkly pigmented subcutaneous or intramuscular nodule
searchTerms: dark soft tissue lump with uneven edges
colored soft tissue growth with irregular shape

pathognomonic.notes: Growth over weeks to months is characteristic

common.symptomName: Localized tenderness or discomfort at lesion site
common.notes: May be present due to mass effect
searchTerms: pain or soreness at lesion site

common.notes: May include satellite lesions or pigmentation spread
searchTerms: darkening or lightening of skin around mass

occasional.notes: Due to nerve involvement or compression
searchTerms: shooting pain along nerves near tumor

occasional.symptomName: Limited range of motion near lesion
occasional.notes: If lesion involves muscle or joint areas

occasional.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss

occasional.notes: Leads to erythema and purulent discharge

rare.symptomName: Distant metastases presenting with respiratory symptoms

rare.notes: Rare but reported in metastatic melanoma
Includes headaches, seizures, or focal deficits
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to brain metastases

laboratory: Elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in advanced disease
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneous soft tissue mass with high signal intensity on T1-weighted images
PET-CT demonstrating metabolic activity and exclusion of other primary sites
Ultrasound of regional lymph nodes for metastasis assessment
other: Histopathology revealing atypical melanocytes with melanin pigment
Immunohistochemical positivity for S-100, HMB-45, and Melan-A

distinguishingFeatures: Different immunohistochemical profile with less consistent melanocytic markers
History or presence of primary cutaneous melanoma
Clinical and imaging evidence of primary skin lesion

redFlags: Rapid enlargement of pigmented soft tissue mass
Presence of regional lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms
references: Orphanet: Melanoma of Soft Tissue, ORPHA:97338
